title: HomeGuard Homeowners Policy — Re-Settlement of Denied Dwelling Water Damage
content:
Under the HomeGuard Homeowners Policy, the dwelling water damage of the most recently reported claim on a HomeGuard policy is re-settled when the claim's first notice records a freeze or a sudden and accidental discharge of water while the dwelling damage stands on the claim only as a repeated-seepage denial entry. This rule fixes the payment that replaces that denial.

## When the rule applies

| Record on the claim | Reading |
|---|---|
| Cause of loss on the first-notice entry | a freeze, or a sudden and accidental discharge of water |
| Dwelling water damage | present on the claim only as a denial entry with the reason repeated seepage |
| Claim concerned | the most recently reported claim on the HomeGuard policy |

The rule governs one result: the amount of the dwelling payment that takes the place of the repeated-seepage denial.

## What the payment records

The replacing payment is one new dwelling payment entry, in the general property class, on the same claim. It carries the replacement-cost value of the denial it replaces, the depreciation recognized, the part of the occurrence deductible it absorbs, the amount paid and the payee. The claim's paid total rises by the amount, and the insured sees a new dwelling payment on the claim file dated the day it is issued.

### Payment kind and payee

- The payment is `replacement_cost_full` when the covered amount is the full replacement-cost value.
- The payment is `acv_initial` otherwise, and the depreciation recognized is withheld on the claim as recoverable depreciation.
- The payee follows the HomeGuard claim settlement payee rule.

## Tool reference: `settle_denied_water_damage_028e176f`

**Capability.** The tool issues the claim payment that replaces a repeated-seepage denial of dwelling water damage on a HomeGuard homeowners claim. One call records one new dwelling payment (general property class) on the named claim. When the payment kind is an actual-cash-value initial payment and depreciation is recognized, that depreciation is withheld on the claim as recoverable depreciation in the same call. The tool records the figures as given; it does not work them out.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `settle_denied_water_damage_028e176f` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `home_policy_id` | Reference number of the HomeGuard policy the claim is made under, as returned by the home policy lookup for the verified customer | identifier |
| `claim_number` | The claim number exactly as it appears on the claim's first-notice entry returned by the claim lookup | copied character for character |
| `source_entry_id` | Reference number of the repeated-seepage denial entry of the dwelling damage that this payment replaces, as returned by the claim lookup | identifier |
| `payment_type` | The kind of dwelling payment | enum: `replacement_cost_full` (paid at full replacement-cost value, nothing withheld) or `acv_initial` (paid at actual cash value, recognized depreciation withheld for later recovery) |
| `depreciation_withheld` | Depreciation recognized on this payment and withheld for recovery | USD, 2 decimal places, 0.00 when nothing is withheld |
| `deductible_applied` | Part of the occurrence deductible absorbed by this payment | USD, 2 decimal places, 0.00 when none |
| `amount` | Amount paid on this dwelling payment | USD, 2 decimal places, positive |
| `payee` | Who the payment is made out to | enum: `insured` (the named insured alone) or `insured_and_mortgagee` (the mortgagee on file named as co-payee with the insured) |

**Return.** On success the tool returns a record with `status` "recorded"; `payment_entry_id` (reference number of the new dwelling payment entry); `claim_number`; `payment_type` (the kind recorded); `amount` (USD, 2 decimal places); `deductible_applied` (USD, 2 decimal places); `depreciation_withheld` (USD, 2 decimal places); `payee`; `holdback_entry_id` (reference number of the recoverable depreciation withheld, or an empty value when nothing was withheld); and `entry_date` (the payment date, YYYY-MM-DD).

### Illustration (hypothetical call)

A hypothetical call passes a policy reference, the claim number as printed on the first notice, the reference of the repeated-seepage denial entry, `payment_type` `acv_initial`, a withheld depreciation, a deductible absorbed, an amount and `payee` `insured`. The receipt shows status "recorded", a new `payment_entry_id` and a `holdback_entry_id` for the depreciation withheld. With `replacement_cost_full` and `depreciation_withheld` 0.00, the `holdback_entry_id` comes back empty.
